worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 28,500.00 = 28,500.00. Federal taxable income = 28,500.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 10,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, single. Line 9 federal AGI 28,500.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 17,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 low- and middle-income worksheet: line 1 28,500.00; line 2 20,000.00; line 3 8,500.00; line 4 0.15; line 5 1,275.00; line 6 2,500.00 - 1,275.00 = 1,225.00; line 7 1 exemption(s); line 8 = 1,225.00. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (single) row for federal AGI 28,500.00 gives 1,000.00 x 1 qualifying = 1,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 1,000.00. Line 17 = 28,500.00 + 0.00 - 17,750.00 - 1,225.00 - 1,000.00 = 8,525.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 10,750.00 = 10,750.00; less base deductions 2,225.00 gives 8,525.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 5,500.00 = 82.5 + 3.2% x 3,025.00 = 96.8; total 179.3, to the cent 179.30. The table row over 8,500 to 8,600 gives 180; expected keeps the formula figure.
